## Key terms

{{< glossary app-package install process loading frame-rate refresh-rate resolution latency bandwidth cloud-gaming thermal-throttling >}}

## 2.1 From the store to the first frame

A game arrives as an **app package** (Android: AAB uploaded to Google Play,
APK on the device; iOS: IPA). **Installation** copies it to storage — no memory
is used yet. Launching creates a **process**, **loads** code and assets from
storage into RAM, starts the engine and the game loop. Loading screens exist
because storage (≈ 0.1–1.5 GB/s) is far slower than RAM. When memory runs
short, the OS terminates background processes — the game restarts from the
title screen.

![Launching a game.](images/launch.png){width=88%}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · Install, launch, load"}
Choose the right term or value.

::: {.match extra="APK|1 s"}
The package format that a developer uploads to Google Play.
:   AAB

The package format of iOS apps.
:   IPA

What installation fills: storage or memory?
:   storage

A program in execution, with its own protected memory.
:   process

The loading time of 1.5 GB of assets at 150 MB/s.
:   10 s

Why a game restarts after a long break in other apps.
:   the OS terminated its process
:::
:::

## 2.2 The frame on real hardware

The **CPU** runs the game logic and prepares drawing commands; the **GPU**
computes the pixels. They work in parallel on consecutive frames, so the
slower one sets the frame time. The player sees at most
min(**frame rate**, **refresh rate**) new images per second. Higher
**resolution** means more pixels for the GPU. Phones have no fan: under
sustained load they slow down (**thermal throttling**).

![CPU and GPU work in parallel on consecutive frames.](images/cpu-gpu-pipeline.png){width=94%}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · Frames, displays, heat"}
Choose the right value or term.

::: {.match extra="120|the GPU"}
A 120 Hz display and a game at 70 fps: new images per second.
:   70

CPU 12 ms and GPU 9 ms per frame: the frame rate.
:   about 83 fps

The processor that limits that game.
:   the CPU

The number of pixels of a 1080 × 2400 screen.
:   about 2.6 million

The chip slows down because it is too hot.
:   thermal throttling
:::
:::

## 2.3 Where the game is computed

**Local**: everything on the device. **Online (client–server)**: each device
runs the game; a server keeps the shared state of the match. **Cloud
gaming**: the game runs on a server; the device sends inputs and plays a video
stream. Cloud gaming needs **bandwidth** (≈ 10–20 Mbit/s for 1080p60) and adds
**latency**: about 44 ms locally becomes about 99 ms with a 40 ms round trip.

![Local, client–server and cloud gaming.](images/where-game-runs.png){width=94%}

{{< sim file="sims/lag-lab.html" poster="sims/lag-lab.png" title="Lag Lab: play with input lag" kind="game" height="560" >}}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · Near or far?"}
Choose the right arrangement or term.

::: {.match extra="local|a card game"}
The game runs entirely on a server; the phone only shows the video.
:   cloud gaming

Each phone runs the game; a server keeps the shared match state.
:   client–server

The delay between an action and its visible result.
:   latency

The amount of data a connection carries per second.
:   bandwidth

Local lag 44 ms + round trip 40 ms + video coding 15 ms.
:   about 99 ms

The kind of game that suffers most from 100 ms of lag.
:   a fighting game
:::
:::

## 2.4 Device classes for gaming

![The five device classes.](images/devices.png){width=92%}

Smartphones and tablets: touch and sensors, battery, no fan, short sessions.
PCs: keyboard, mouse or gamepad, the widest range of performance. Consoles:
gamepad, TV, fixed high performance. Cloud gaming: any screen, but a fast
network. A game designed for one class must be adapted — input, screen,
session length and power — before it works on another.

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 4 · Which device class?"}
Choose the device class.

::: {.match extra="embedded system"}
Gamepad, TV, fixed high performance.
:   console

Keyboard and mouse, the widest range of performance.
:   PC

Touch, battery, no fan, five-minute sessions in a pocket.
:   smartphone

Any screen, as long as the network is fast.
:   cloud gaming
:::
:::

## Game challenge: the class survey {.challenge}

Work alone. Use every section of today.

A first-year class lists the devices it plays on. Most students use Android
phones of different prices; the cheapest one reads its storage at 120 MB/s. A
few use iPhones and some use laptops. One student has a console. Two play
through a cloud gaming service; one of them has a round trip of 90 ms to the
data centre. The class wants one game that runs on all of these devices.

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 5 · One game, many devices (harder)"}
Use the numbers of the survey and of today's sections.

::: {.match extra="0.2 s|99 ms"}
The loading time of a 600 MB level on the cheapest phone.
:   5 s

The input lag of the cloud player with the 90 ms round trip.
:   149 ms

The input device of the student with the console.
:   gamepad

The device class where thermal throttling matters most in a 30-minute session.
:   smartphone

The package format of the iPhone version.
:   IPA
:::
:::

## Summary {.summary}

- Install = copy to storage; launch = create a process and load into RAM.
- Storage speed decides loading time; memory decides what stays loaded.
- CPU and GPU work in parallel; the slower sets the frame rate; the display caps it.
- Phones throttle under sustained load.
- Local, client–server, cloud: cloud adds latency and needs bandwidth.
- Each device class needs its own input, layout and performance plan.
